newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PALMEIRAS LOSE OUT TO GREMIO AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PALMEIRAS LOSE OUT TO GREMIO AGAIN.

text.p: Brazilian championship favourites Palmeiras were knocked out of the competition by Gremio on Sunday, the third time in two years they have been eliminated from a major tournament by their arch-rivals.
Palmeiras, who finished the first stage of the competition five points ahead of Gremio, won their quarter-final, second leg 1-0 at home but went out 3-2 on aggregate.

Last year, Gremio knocked Palmeiras out of both the South American Libertadores Cup and the Copa Brasil, although Palmeiras gained some revenge this year by beating Gremio in the Copa Brasil after fate once again paired the two teams.

Palmeiras, who scored 102 goals on their way to winning the Sao Paulo championship in the first half of the year, scored in the 75th minute through substitute Elivelton but created few other chances against a determined Gremio defence.

Rivalry between the two clubs has often been bitter, with three players sent off and a 20-minute brawl halting the first leg of their Libertadores Cup tie and four sendings-off in one of last year's Copa Brasil clashes.
On Sunday, there was a skirmish just before halftime while Gremio striker Saulo, having already been booked, was sent off for playing on after the referee had whistled for offside.
Three players had been sent off in Wednesday's first leg.

The other three quarter-finals were also won by the teams with poorer record in the first stage as Portuguesa overcame first-stage winners Cruzeiro, Goias knocked out Guarani and Atletico Mineiro beat Atletico Paranaense.

The 24 teams in the Brazilian championship play each other once in the first stage with the top eight progressing. In the knockout stages, the teams with the better first stage record goes through if the aggregate scores are level but apart from that have nothing to show for their better overall record.
Cruzeiro finished the first stage eight points clear of Portuguesa, who sneaked into the quarter-finals on the last day when two rivals lost, only to lose 3-0 in Wednesday's first leg.
Cruzeiro won the second leg 1-0 with a goal by striker Cleisson but never looked like making up the difference.
Guarani went out 3-2 on aggregate to Goias, who finished the first stage six points below them, after winning 1-0 on Sunday.
Ailton scored in the third minute but Guarani's hopes took a severe knock when striker Gilson was sent off before halftime for a tackle from behind.
Atletico Paranaense beat Atletico Mineiro 1-0 but went out 3-2 on aggregate.
